System Map

Read together, the five themes describe one question: when something goes wrong, whose balance sheet takes the hit. Four loops connect them. Forced sales feed falling prices (R1): a fall in AI shares prompts withdrawals, and funds that sell to meet them push prices down further. Queues prompt more requests (R2): withdrawal limits leave a queue that gives savers a reason to ask early. Higher yields bring buyers back (B1): as patient buyers of government bonds step back, yields rise until some return. Refunds push prevention upstream (B2): rules that make platforms and phone networks share scam losses give them a reason to stop scams.

AI and funds		A fall in AI share prices prompts withdrawal requests, funds sell to meet them, and the sales push prices down further.Priming: holdings and leverage up, no fall yet

Private credit		Requests above the withdrawal limit leave a queue, and the queue gives savers a reason to ask early, which lengthens it.Turning: requests near 10% against a 5% cap, though easing

Government bonds		Fewer patient buyers push long-term yields up, and higher yields bring some buyers back, which steadies them.Priming: some buyers return at 4% in Japan
B2Refunds push prevention upstream
Payment losses		Scam losses carried by banks lead to rules that make platforms and phone networks share the cost, and sharing the cost pushes prevention to where scams start, which cuts losses.Turning: refund rules in the UK, the EU and Australia

Hover over a status for its meaning: Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale. Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks whether loops R1 and R2 end with savers or with the state: whether savers carry the losses of forced sales and queues, or a widened safety net does. Its vertical axis asks whether money keeps moving freely, or whether national controls, an outside switch on the map, keep it in national lanes.

What it means: no organisation can stop a fall in AI shares or a government’s borrowing, but each can keep money out of the queue in loop R2, test what loop R1 would sell first, write loss-sharing terms that decide how loop B2 runs, and keep track of the controls that switch routes on and off.
